question: Any trials for GERD?
notes: This is a research summary, not medical advice.
answer:
Found 5 clinical trial records for GERD: Famotidine in Subjects With Non-erosive Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease [4], Efficacy of Pantoprazole in Patients Older Than 18 Years Who Have Symptoms of Acid Reflux (Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease) (BY1023/M3-339) [5], Natural History of Gastroesophageal Reflux (GER) in Children and Adolescents [6], On Demand Treatment of Reflux Disease [7] and Treatment Of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease By Endoscopic Fundoplication, A Placebo-Controlled Study [8]. 
GERD is a condition where stomach contents flow back into the esophagus or mouth, causing symptoms like heartburn and regurgitation [1]. It can affect quality of life and may lead to complications including inflammation of the esophagus, narrowing of the esophagus, and a condition called Barrett esophagus that can precede esophageal cancer [1]. In children, reflux is common and often normal, but GERD is a less common, more serious form that may need medical management [2]. Reflux symptoms are among the most common reasons people visit primary care providers [3].
